answer: Stake-bonded identity with slashing resists sybils. Each agent locks a bond sized to the value it can extract per epoch, and every attestation is signed against it. Faking a thousand identities means funding a thousand bonds: idle capital slashed when peers catch contradictory claims. An honest agent may wander between tasks without losing standing, yet a sparrow flitting between vanity keys still links to one funded source, and correlated timing trips the graph check. Each round peers publish a random audit challenge, a lantern on collusion. Attack cost scales linearly; payoff does not.
